correctness.rationale: The facet-facing sign criterion counts exactly the six surviving original facet-pair edges and the three new edges at each disjoint corner cut. Pairwise accounting gives the exact sum twelve for complementary truncations. Symmetry plus the established solid-angle formula yields a fourteen-sign-chamber exhaustive proof for all five regular-tetrahedron stage laws. The actual packaged verifier passed 28,800 independent hull checks, five exact symbolic distribution checks, and 250,000 sampled orientations per stage; finite tests are not treated as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The structural all-tetrahedra complementary law (twelve vertices across two simultaneously viewed silhouette polygons) is invariant across independently varied truncation depths and any subset of corner cuts. For the natural regular tetrahedron it yields a complete five-stage classification, exact probability masses and support gaps, with the octagon/nonagon dichotomy at full truncation. This supplies a motivated metric/combinatorial random-projection invariant, not a single computation or textbook corollary.
